diet.text: Lizards, birds and their eggs, frogs

overview.text: The Boomslang is a slender, highly venomous tree snake of sub-Saharan Africa. Unlike most of its family, the colubrids, its bite can kill a person. Its venom acts slowly: symptoms may not appear until many hours after a bite.

identification.text: A slim snake with very large eyes with round pupils, giving it sharp eyesight. Colour varies from plain brown to green; males are usually more colourful than females.

variation.label: Sexes
variation.text: Males tend to be brighter; female hatchlings are pale brown.

behaviour.text: An active hunter in trees and bushes that relies on its excellent vision. Its fangs are at the back of the mouth (it is "rear-fanged").

diet.text: Lizards, birds, bird eggs and frogs, which it swallows whole after biting.

funfacts.text: In 1957 the famous American herpetologist Karl Patterson Schmidt died after being bitten by a young boomslang.
